No, the answers are not better. I'd hold off on merging. I ran the eval harness (`python -m evals.run --set golden`) at commit `3ae9d6e` and compared it with the saved 512-token baseline. Retrieval improved slightly, but answer quality, latency and cost all got worse.

| Metric | Baseline (512) | Current (1024) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recall@5 | 0.933 | 0.967 | +0.034 |
| MRR | 0.933 | 0.933 | 0 |
| Faithfulness (judge `example-judge-v1`, same for both) | 0.907 | 0.838 | **−0.069** |
| Latency p50 | 1.16 s | 1.77 s | **+53%** |
| Latency p95 | 1.48 s | 3.40 s | **+130%** |
| Cost per query | $0.0111 | $0.0167 | **+50%** |
| Failing questions | q07, q19 | q07, q12, q21, q30 | 1 fixed, 3 new |

**New failures (I looked at all three):**
- **q12, q21, q30:** The search finds the right datasheet section and ranks it first. The model still answers "roughly double the datasheet value" instead of the actual value (expected 36, 63 and 90 units), and faithfulness scores 0.55. So these are failures in writing the answer, not in finding the source. A likely cause is that bigger chunks put more unrelated text in front of the model, but the test data's chunk text is placeholder, so I can't confirm that from the content.

**Still failing:**
- **q07:** None of the five retrieved chunks is a correct source, but the answer is still right ("21 units"). That means the model answered without support from what it retrieved, possibly from memory, or the grading is off. This was already failing at 512, so it isn't caused by this change.

**Fixed:**
- **q19:** It failed in the baseline and passes now. This is the only gain.

**Verdict: REGRESSED.** Recall improved by one question. In exchange, faithfulness drops by about 7 points, three answers become wrong even though the right source was found, p95 latency more than doubles, and cost per query goes up 50%.

Before merging, you could try 1024-token chunks with fewer chunks per query (smaller top-k) to bring back faithfulness and cost. Another option is staying at 512 and adding a reranker to recover q19.

I left the baseline (`evals/baselines/main.json`) unchanged. The run's results are in `evals/results/latest.json`.
